chunks: He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad -- may God have mercy on him -- reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdul Karim ibn Amru and Ibrahim ibn Rahah al-Basri, who both narrated from Mayassar, who said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, said to me:

"What do you say about a person who does not disobey God in His commands and prohibitions, except that he disassociates from you and your companions regarding this matter?" I said: "What can I say while I am in your presence?" He said: "Say! For I am the one who commands you to speak." I said: "He is in the Fire."

He said: "O Mayassar! What do you say about a person who worships God with the same faith as yours, and has sins like other people, except that he avoids the major sins?" I said: "What can I say while I am in your presence?" He said: "Say! For I am the one who commands you to speak." I said: "In Paradise." He said: "Perhaps you hesitate to say he is in Paradise?" I said: "No." He said: "Then do not hesitate, for he is in Paradise."
"Indeed God, Almighty and Exalted, says: 'If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We shall expiate your evil deeds from you and admit you to a noble entrance.'" (Quran 4:31)

key_terms.الكبائر: Major sins (al-kaba'ir) -- grave transgressions whose avoidance guarantees forgiveness of lesser sins
key_terms.ولاية: Wilayah -- allegiance and loyalty to the Ahlul Bayt, considered the foundational pillar of faith
key_terms.يبرأ: Disassociation (bara'ah) -- rejecting or severing ties with the rightful authorities

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about someone who obeys God but rejects the wilayah of Ahlul Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith narrated from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) through Mayassar presents a striking theological dialogue about the centrality of wilayah (allegiance to the Ahlul Bayt). The Imam poses two contrasting cases: a person who obeys God's commands but rejects the wilayah, and a person who has the correct faith (including wilayah) but commits minor sins. The Imam rules that the first is in the Fire and the second is in Paradise, citing Quran 4:31 as proof that God forgives minor sins for those who avoid major ones -- and implicitly, that rejecting wilayah is a major sin that outweighs all other obedience.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 4. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad - may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his father, from Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdul Karim ibn Amru and Ibrahim ibn Rahah al-Basri, who both reported from Mayassar, who reported that: Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him told him:

"What do you say about a person who does not disobey in what Allah has enjoined and forbidden, but he disassociates with you and your friends in this matter (i.e. wilayah of Ahlul Bayt)?" I said: "What can I say in your presence?" He said: "Say, for I command you to speak." I said: "He will be in hellfire."

Then he said: "O Mayassar, what do you say about a person who has faith similar to yours, and has committed sins normally committed by people, but he refrains from the major sins?" I said: "What can I say in your presence?" He said: "Say, for that is my order." I said: "He will be in Paradise." He said: "Perhaps you are hesitating in saying that such a person will be in Paradise!" I said: "No" He said: "Do not hesitate, for surely,
Allah, Most High, says (in the Qur’an): ’If you avoid the heinous sins that are forbidden you, We will expiate your evil deeds and admit you in honourable manner.’ (al-Nisa, 4:31)"
